name: zebu
author: logic-agent
description: PRIVATE. Zebra-puzzle-lite: five items A-E in five positions 1-5. Clue = 4-7 space-separated 3-character constraints in a tiny language, all true of a hidden target arrangement and jointly forcing it to be UNIQUE: 'A<B' = A is somewhere left of B, 'A|B' = A and B are adjacent, 'C#3' = C sits at position 3 (1-indexed); at most two '#' constraints per clue so the ordering operators carry the puzzle. Solution = a 5-letter permutation of ABCDE read as 'the letter standing at position 1,2,3,4,5' (NOT the position of each letter - the inverse permutation is the classic wrong guess and scores 0). DIFFICULTY: hard. DISCOVERY PATH: three constraint shapes have to be reverse-engineered from a handful of clues plus one demo. '#' is the easiest ('C#3' with a demo answer whose 3rd letter is C pins both the operator AND the position convention in one shot), then '<' from an instance where the demo answer orders the pair, then '|'. Gradient: a team that handles only '#' and '<' and brute-forces the 120 permutations still scores on every instance whose '|' constraints happen to be implied; a team that guesses the inverse convention scores ~0, which is itself a loud signal. Brute force over 5! = 120 arrangements makes the search trivial once the language is known - the whole difficulty is the language.
